Only 22% of remote job listings state a pay figure. The other 78%? They're marked DOE (determined on experience) — meaning the salary is set only after the employer reviews your résumé.

Out of 4,280 active remote listings on Loker Dollar, just 940 disclose a concrete USD figure, while 3,340 leave the pay blank. That doesn't have to be a red flag. In fields like AI development and specialized healthcare, a DOE label can push offers above market averages for the strongest candidates.

Three ways to turn a hidden figure into leverage:
1. Research global benchmarks for your role before you talk numbers.
2. Quantify your impact — revenue uplift, cost savings — so you can justify the high end.
3. Anchor with a range and ask about total compensation (equity, bonuses, benefits), not just base pay.

One real example: Online Consumer Panels America lists $25–$45/hour for product assessments. Rates like that exist — you just have to know where to look. 64% of listings (2,735) accept applicants from any country.

Full breakdown and the negotiation playbook: https://lokerdollar.com/en/blog/what-is-doe-wage
